questions.q: Who sets Bank Rate in the UK?
questions.why: The Bank has been independent on this since 1997.
The government sets the target, and the Bank decides how to meet it.

questions.q: What does "lender of last resort" mean?
options: The central bank lends to banks in a crisis
Banks lend only to rich people
questions.why: It helps to stop a bank run from spreading.

questions.q: A change in Bank Rate has its full effect on inflation straight away.
questions.why: It can take up to about two years.

questions.q: Which would most likely lead the MPC to cut Bank Rate?
options: Forecast inflation well below 2% and a weak economy

questions.q: Explain why an independent central bank may be better at controlling inflation.

ideas.label: It's free from short-term political pressure
So it's more credible, which keeps inflation expectations low

questions.model: An independent bank is free from short-term political pressure, such as elections. This makes the target more credible, so inflation expectations stay low.
questions.why: People believe a target that politicians can't bend.

tests.answer: It is free from political pressure, so its target is credible and expectations stay low.
It is free from political pressure.
